utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-09-92-T, The Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The Chamber was informed that there was one preliminary about scheduling. Or is there not? There seems to be -- yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. On Friday, we received your decision to work extended hours on Monday and Tuesday. We discussed the issue with Mr. Mladic. Objectively speaking, he is not able to attend the extended sessions because of his health condition. That's why the Defence team decided to better organise our cross-examination, because we did prepare in advance both the documents and the intended length of our examination. So this is to put you on notice that for the next witness, RM511, we plan to have our cross-examination last five hours. For the upcoming witness, Mr. Thomas, the cross-examination would last two and a half hours, and the following witness in this week, RM087, Ms. Birte Weiss, the cross-examination would last one and a half hours. Based on these estimates, we believe that we have cut down our initial estimate by four to five hours. On that basis, we do not believe that it will be necessary to work the extended afternoon sessions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Have you discussed the matter with the Prosecution, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, we announced that we would be cutting down our estimates to the Prosecution on Friday afternoon. This morning, they issued us again with a preliminary schedule of witnesses, and the reduced it time for cross-examination of Mr. Thomas and Birte Weiss was something that we worked on over the weekend and were not able to inform them about it this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I suggest that Mr. Stojanovic and myself speak at the first break. Perhaps some information did not reach me, but I will do some calculations and advise the Chamber at the start of the next session on my views of whether or not we need the extended sessions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And of course the Chamber will think about it as well. For the -- we'll discuss it during the first break as well. Then if there's no other matter to be discussed before the witness enters the courtroom, could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. And, due to face distortion, the curtains need to be down for a minute.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour, good morning. As he is being brought in, if I could go head and begin making a record of the adjudicated facts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: There are a number of adjudicated facts upon which the Prosecution relied in deciding to redact certain portions of the tendered statements including, 2037, 2045, 2065, 2134, 2571, 2845, and 2852. Additionally there are a number of adjudicated facts upon which we relied in deciding not to tender certain document and not to elicit information during the direct examination in consideration of your Your Honours' 2nd May 2012 fourth decision on Prosecution motion for judicial notice of adjudicated facts concerning the rebuttal evidence procedure. So in addition to the ones already listed above these would be in regard to Incident F-11: 2297, 2299, 2300, 2302 through 2304.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: In regard to G-13: 2546, 2548, 2549, 2554 and 2555. In regard to G-15: 2564, 2571, 2576 through 78, 2580. In addition to the shelling incident on 28th June of 1995 of the TV building: 2834, 2835, 2844 through 2846. And with regard to that incident specifically, Your Honour, the Prosecution is refraining from entering into evidence 65 ter number 10167 which is listed on our exhibit notification for this witness. In regard to the shelling incident on Geteova street on 28 June 1995, that would be adjudicated fact 2849, 2849, 2852. And with regard to this incident, Your Honours, the Prosecution would like to specifically point to 65 ter numbers 10210 and 103 -- I'm sorry, 13865, the latter being an associate exhibit which we referenced on Friday. Both documents on our exhibit notification list for this witness which we are refraining from tendering for last incident based on the adjudicated facts, and I'm sorry for the length of that record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and apart from that also for the speed of speech, I take it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, I apologise for that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness RM110.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is not very polite to continue to speak when you're entering the courtroom. This is not a criticism, Ms. Hochhauser. It's just -- just to the witness. Witness RM110, I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony last Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Hochhauser will now continue her examination-in-chief. Please listen carefully to her questions. Please proceed, Ms. Hochhauser.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Good morning, RM110.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm going to turn now to some questions about G-18, the bombing of the Markale market on 28 August 1995. If we could, Your Honours, please go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Turning -- can we please turn to page 27 of this -- of these photographs -- this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And, sir, the pictures at page -- pages 27, and then also 28 and 29, the following two photographs, does this accurately depict the damaged mortar stabiliser recovered at the entrance of the Markale market on the 28th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the stabiliser of a mortar shell. It was also found on the scene.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I -- I would like to tender 10288 [sic] into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, there is apparently something wrong with your microphone. Could that be -- could you please repeat and could you carefully check whether we have the right number, the right 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's -- one second.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's now better.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter number that was this photo is 10228, and it's assigned number P499.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence as a public exhibit. Yes, and we now see that the reference, as we find it in the transcript, on page 13, line 7, which was a mistake, is now corrected on page 13, line 16. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time I would like to play the entirety of Exhibit P446 which was entered into evidence during the testimony of a previous witness but only a very small segment of it was played. The video is approximately seven minutes and 15 seconds long and that would conclude my examination -- I'm sorry. I would have one question after it and then that would conclude my examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed. You do not rely on text.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: May I, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Sir, in the first portion of that video, we see -- we see what appeared to be a -- civilians moving -- moving the bodies out of the scene. Is that what you were describing earlier in your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Before -- I've never seen this video before.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Sir, did you -- did you have an opportunity to review this video prior to coming to court the other day over the -- last week?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, last week. I'm sorry. I mean, I meant the earlier period, before I came here. I didn't mean the period since I've been here.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And the first portion of that video where we see the bodies of victims being removed from the scene, you were not present for that; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was not present then.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And how about the latter part of the video where we see once the victims have been removed?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. By that time, I was already there, and I do recognise these people. That is to say, the team from the international force. I think

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. If the parties are discussing scheduling issues over the next break, the Chamber would encourage that you'd come up with a detailed plan, because if we start with concerns about whether we could conclude our whole programme for this week and if then it's just a matter of, We'll take less time, we'd like to know exactly what day, what session, for what witness, and for the Chamber to accept a solution as suggested by the Mladic Defence, a detailed schedule would certainly assist. We take a break, and we'll resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We perhaps first deal with scheduling issues. Could I hear from the parties -- by the way, Mr. Groome, I take it that you have been informed about the fact that the Chamber noted that three and a half plus one and a half is five instead of four, as was seen on last week's schedule.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I believe we've --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which means that the schedule you prepared would amount to 20 and a half hours rather than 19 and a half. Could I hear from the parties. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. We just discussed the scheduling issue, and we divided it into days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So we should start tomorrow with RM511.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He should be finished by the end of Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then we have Thursday for RM171.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me have a look. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And if necessary it can be finished on Friday, because, now, for RM087 in total, we have Prosecution and the Defence two and a half hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two and a half.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. So we are pretty confident that all these witnesses can be finished in this week without having any extended sittings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, now, Mr. Groome, that would be today for RM110 without extra sessions. Would Witness RM511 be available already to start if we would ...

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So that is today, that's Monday. Tuesday, Wednesday for Witness RM511. Thursday for Witness RM171. Would one day be sufficient?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably. But, if necessary, we can take one hour from Friday as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And Friday then would still remain sufficient time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber is -- is willing to follow the suggestion made by the parties, but it's -- now and then happens that unexpected things arrive. I mean, this will then be a tight schedule. And if these things happen both parties commit themselves to limited time in such a way, I mean, if we are half an hour -- if there's a power cut, you'll have to resolve that. We're not going to change it in any other way. The Chamber has made three hours extra available and expects the parties to conclude this programme this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I agreed with Mr. Groome, if it fits Your Honour, if necessary which might have Friday extension if necessary, but we doubt that it would be the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, but, of course --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If there's a power cut, we cannot control power cut.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand that. But Friday it is just impossible. Not all Judges are available, so that would be a problem. And I add to this, Mr. Lukic, that the Chamber is happy to follow the -- the schedule as suggested by the parties. The Chamber, however, by doing this, does not implicitly accept the health reasons which are claimed. At this moment we have no medical reports which would support that, neither has the Chamber observed itself anything which would give further support to that. So although agreeing with the suggestion, it's on the basis of an agreement and a commitment of the parties not on the basis of health issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Can I just say the following. That this -- this schedule is made possible by revised estimates of cross-examination by the Defence. I cannot commit to less time in direct examination, although the Prosecution always endeavours to take the minimum amount of time. Could I suggest to the Chamber that in order to plan for the possibility of something unforeseen, that the extra time now scheduled for tomorrow not be foregone or not cancelled until we see tomorrow how things have gone and -- if that's possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me check for one second with Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we'll proceed as suggested. Could the curtains be down. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. And, Mr. Stojanovic, after all that's done, you may continue with your cross-examination. But I think we have to move -- do we still have to move in private session, Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the document that we will be using is under seal, and only the first few questions need to be put in private session. And then, after that, we can move into open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We now move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: While we're waiting for the document to be uploaded - but I think we can see it now - I would like to ask you if you're able to recognise this area.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can recognise it. This is part of the Svrakino Selo neighbourhood.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I would now kindly ask the usher to hand you a marker so that you can circle the building that was hit by a modified air bomb on that occasion, according to your best recollection.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can I now ask you to mark the right-hand side of the circle with an MB, modified bomb.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. And now please mark the RTV Dom building, the federal television building, if you see it in this photograph. Could you mark the building with a circle?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And can you mark the circle with a RTV?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. What do you think, how far is this building from the RTV Dom that was hit by this modified air bomb?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as the crow flies, I -- I really couldn't be very specific. Perhaps it could be a couple of hundred metres. Perhaps not even that much. But, really, I -- I could not say exactly.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If you can see it in this photograph, could you please mark the police station in the formerly Prvomajska Ulica Street. If you can see it in this area?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot really see it very well. All you can see here are roofs. So you cannot really see the police station building clearly.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, I know. But if I can just ask you to mark the roof with a circle.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it should be somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If I may ask you to -- oh, we've lost it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. All the markings apparently are lost. Madam Registrar, any technical solution for this?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If I could also ...

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If I could just add to that, Your Honour, all of our middle monitors have gone out so we're unable to follow the evidence and the markings at the moment. If somebody could come assist us. I don't want to stop the examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Perhaps we use the time, meanwhile, to have the old markings to be done again. Could you again with the assistance of the usher with the ... Could -- could ... could the usher assist the witness in marking again, first, where the modified air bomb landed; that is, the marking was close to where G-13 is. Witness, could you please be so kind to mark that again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you add the letters there, modified air bomb, MB again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you now mark again the radio/TV station, as you did before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And add the letters you wrote there before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could you now -- what is visible from the police station even if it's only partial, could you mark that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You can just see roofs on this building. So that would be here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If I may ask you to mark that circle with a PS, police station.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the police station located in the same building in May 1991?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And are you able to mark, according to your best recollection, where the cannon shells, as you said, fell in the then-street of Safeta Hadzica. Can you please mark approximately more or less that area.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You cannot really see it, but there is an area behind these four buildings. To the right, there was a school, so I could perhaps just draw a line approximately where that was. But you cannot see the ground where that happened.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes. Could you then please mark it in the way that you've indicated.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: So roughly beyond these buildings here, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. To the best of your recollection, what was the distance between the impact points of these shells and the police station?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell that you. After all, we didn't even measure that distance; that's to say, the distance between the police station and the point where the projectiles impacted the ground.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, I would like to tender page 39 of P3 as marked here as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number of the photograph marked by the witness would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Would be D95, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. Mr. Stojanovic, do we have to stay in -- oh, we are in open session, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Sir, before we remove the document from our screens, let me ask you this: These shells, regardless of how many there were, and the modified air bomb, did they impact the ground roughly at the same time, in your view?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With hindsight, can I tell you that they impacted at very short intervals of time. You could even say that they hit the ground almost at the same time. Of course, I'm giving you information that we got from eye-witnesses who were there at the scene.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And did they all come from the same direction?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I remember, they did. But you have the direction from which they came, all of them, contained in my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'd like us to look at it again. At P45 -- or, rather, P495. And let me remind you again that it's under seal, but I do believe we could stay in open session, until a point, at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, not to be broadcast, but we can discuss it in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us look at page 2 in both versions. Page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Sir, we will be now following roughly the answers that you gave earlier on. Please look at paragraph 2 of the report which reads: "Based on the recovered unexploded projectiles and parts of the exploded projectiles that were recovered, it was established that in all these cases the same armour-piercing explosive artillery projectiles were used of 90-millimetre calibre produced in the Nazi Germany and bearing the following marks." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: This is my question: Who established that the calibre in question was 90 millimetres? Please don't give us the name, only the function.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that it was the individual under number 3 who was a member of the crime-scene examination team and these were the findings that he arrived at at the scene. Of course, all these various elements were certainty to the Ministry of Interior to the KDZ department for their final examination and ultimate analysis.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did that same individual also provided the information contained in this report to the effect that they were armour-piercing explosive artillery projectiles?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that too.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Who is behind the statement that in all these listed cases - and based on my calculations they were ten plus 1, that's to say, 11 - the same artillery piece of the same calibre was used which was produced in the Nazi Germany?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "who is behind the statement"? Do you mean the sentence written in the report or are you asking about what it was that the person under number 3 established at the scene?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I will formulate my question slightly differently. You will see that it reads here: It was established that in all the listed cases the same artillery piece indicated here was used. Who was it? Who established this?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received information about it from the individual under number 3, and I included it in my report. As I said earlier, the information was obtained at the scene during the crime-scene examination. All these various elements were then forwarded on for final forensic examination and definitive findings.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Very well. Let me ask you this: Is my understanding of this report correct; i.e., that all these shells that were listed in the paragraph above in fact 90-millimetre armour-piercing explosive artillery projectiles produced in the Nazi Germany?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All of them or, rather, this qualification here applies to all those projectiles listed above, because the damage and the traces found at the scene all came from the same type of shell, the same type of weapon, except for the second paragraph where you see that they say that the damage comes from an unidentified weapon which fired from the westerly direction.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: This was supposed to be my next question but let us just establish this. You were not able to ascertain the weapon which might have fired such shells as were qualified here as the 90-millimetre artillery pieces from Germany?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not myself. I wasn't an expert in that area. I only related the information I received from the individual under number 3. So I repeat: This is not my own formation.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I didn't find anywhere in this report or note that you weren't able to say with any certainty what the distance of fire was.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I said, I wasn't trained for this sort of work. Had anybody been able to establish the distance from which fire was opened, I would probably have included that information in my report.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I will conclude with this question. To the best of your recollection, can you tell how far removed was the front line between the Army of Republika Srpska and the BH army from the point or from the scene which you examined?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't tell you that because I was never present at the front line. I never had an opportunity to go there.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: This same report in the next paragraph states that the shells were fired from an unidentified weapon from the westerly direction which would correspond to the positions of the insurgent Serbs in the area of Ilidza. Now, whose statement was this?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was made by the person under number 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me -- let me just -- does the document say "insurgent" or "aggressor," the original?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, I'm reading from the B/C/S version which says "insurgent Bosnian Serbs" or "rebel Bosnian Serbs."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: While we have the document here, let's look at page 12 of the B/C/S and 11 of the English version of the document. While we're waiting for it to appear, let me ask you a few things about the document. You say that the fragments of the shells that you were able to find at the scene, you seized and sent on for further forensic examination which was how the rules governed it; right?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: In the document before us which was authored by the Ministry of Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina Anti-Sabotage Department, on the basis of a forensic examination of the elements that you sent them, they established that, in their view - and if you can see this in paragraph 1 - it most probably involved a contact-fuse high-explosive shell, 88 millimetres in calibre. Will you agree with me that in forensic examination is contrary to what the individual who provided information for the other report arrived at?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if it was contrary. At any rate, what I do know is that this is what the Ministry of Interior established. The fact that there's a difference calibre ... well, is this report by the Ministry of Interior the final one?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: If I were to tell you that following consultation with experts in this field, there is no such thing as the armour-piercing explosive projectile. If I were to tell you this, would you then agree with what you see here?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't go into that. I have not had the appropriate training. I am not an expert in this field.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us look at this document, the last page, which reads, and this is what the team of experts say, "that an analysis of the fragments taken from the scene," can we stay with the same document, please, "established." That's page 12 of the B/C/S and 11 of the English versions, P495. Thank you. Yes, that's the document. It reads that the members of this MUP department, the BH MUP department, established that this shell, this type of projectile, was of an earlier date and was one that could be found in the JNA arsenal. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that what we read here is, yet again, contrary to what the Official Note says; i.e., that all the shells that were fired were of the same origin, of the -- of the same calibre, and had come from Germany?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The report stated that it was produced at that time; whereas this document here only says that it was to be found in the former JNA arsenal but did not refer to its date of manufacture.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that the shells which originally came from Germany and dated back to World War II were present in the JNA arsenal after the war?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not what I said. You asked me what the documents differed in, and I told you what they differed in. The report stated where the weapons had been manufactured, and this document states that they were in the JNA arsenal. I didn't state one or the other, simply because, as I said already, I'm not an expert in the field. I'm not able to give you any details about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Will you agree with me that the weaponry that belonged to the former JNA could also be found in the BH army?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I don't know what type of weapons there were. I didn't have any such contacts. I wasn't at the front line. And I didn't know what sort of weapons the army had. I was a policeman, and I only did policing work.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now look at P497 in e-court; photograph number 1. Can we blow it up, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Sir, does this document reflect the impact site of one of the shells addressed in the notes as a result of a forensic examination?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: You had an opportunity to see this photograph before you testified; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Could you please tell me, to the best of your recollection and to the extent to which you can see, the central part marked with an arrow, is that the point of impact of one of these shells that you recorded in your document?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I think that that is one of the points of impact.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that the roof of this auxiliary building was built of a light material that we know as "salonit"?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say exactly. It is covered with snow here, and given the time that has gone by, I cannot recall what the roof was made of.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Sir, I did not quite understand you. You said that it was covered with snow?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that what it seems like to me from here. Well, practically there was any snow. Something white. Perhaps this was a slip on my part. It's sort of white. I cannot see what it is made of, and of course there couldn't have been any snow at the time. I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm asking you all of this because of the following, if you can give me an answer, on the basis of all of the experiences that you've had with these on-site investigations: Is it possible if a shell, the way you described it in either one of the two reports after the expertise, in view of the point of impact that we see here on the photograph, is it possible that due to the impact wave it does not disturb the roof at all, regardless of the material that was used to make the roof? On the basis of your experience, would that be possible?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I don't want to go into this kind of assessment or estimates because I'm not that familiar with the area. I cannot really discuss this field competently. I think that this needs to be dealt with by an expert.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I'm going to ask you, bearing in mind the marking of buildings that you conducted and that we saw in that photograph, in war time, is a police station a legitimate military target?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I'm not a military analyst and this is not something that I'm very familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I will conclude with the following question: The RTV centre, although you're not a military analyst, in your view is that a legitimate military target? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by this, "legitimate military target." I don't see what you mean when you say that. Could you please explain that to me. In any rate it seems to me that my answer would be the same. I cannot say what a legitimate military target is and what it is not.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. My understanding is that you carried out on-site investigations in several places where modified air bombs, as you called them, fell; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Did your experience lead to you a situation in which you would realise that such a projectile could ricochet?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not go into any such thing. I'm telling you yet again: It is experts who conveyed information to me as to how an explosion took place, whether it happened in this or that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we see P495 again. I would like to remind you of the fact that it is under seal, although we'll be using pages 2 in both versions. I believe that we can remain in open court. Thank you for your assistance. And ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You mean not to be broadcasted but can still be discussed. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: So this is what I asked you: To the best of your recollection, all of the shells on that date, did they come from the same direction? And you said: As far as I can remember, yes. But I would like to see the document. And now I would just like to direct you to this. According to this document, according to the record, shells arrived from the west, which would correspond to the area of Ilidza. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: In the last paragraph on this page in B/C/S - and could I please have the next page in English - this is what it says when describing the analysis of the modified projectile trajectory: It is established that it was fired from a south, southwesterly direction corresponding to the aggressor positions of the rebel Bosnian Serbs in the Lukavica area. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not the rebel Bosnian Muslims. It's the rebel Bosnian Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I do apologise. The rebel Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that and I will go back to what I said a moment ago. As far as I can remember, that's the way it was. And I would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second. Do we have the same in English as we have in ... Oh, yes. It's the bottom, the very last -- let me see, yes. Yes, I see it. Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Please go ahead. Perhaps you have been interrupted. You wanted to say something in relation to the direction from which these projectiles came.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said, as far as I can remember, in relation to your first question, I would like to see this document and now I see the document, and it is certainly the way it was. It is the way I wrote it down when it happened. That is a fact that was established on the spot at that point in time. When I gave my first answer, I said "to the best of my recollection." But what is correct is what is stated here in the report, both.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: So it would be correct to say that shells and explosive devices that fell on that occasion had not come from the same direction.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the way it would be. That is what was established, too; that is to say, the west and south-west.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Appreciating the point of impact of these shells, can you tell the Chamber what the distance is between the area of Ilidza and the area of Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly, as I've already said in relation to the distance between the housing facility and the television building. At any rate, it's not a major distance as the crow flies; that is, if you look at the boundaries of the municipality of Ilidza and the neighbourhood of Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: As for this event that we discussed now, you said that there had been material damage and also that some persons were injured; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see that in my report. I assume that I did establish that, and if I established it then that is correct. I cannot see it. I cannot see the page where that is stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, may we please take a look at page 3 in B/C/S and in English as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And now if we look at the second paragraph in B/C/S where it says: "Several persons were injured and the surrounding buildings extensively damaged in the explosion of a modified explosive projectile which hit the roof," et cetera. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: This is what I'm asking you now: All the persons that are listed here were they injured by that projectile of the modified air bomb or are these person who had been injured by all the shells that were fired on that day within that period of time?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember exactly now. But roughly what was stated was that this was due to the projectile that fell on the roof. I can just confirm that what I established is correct, as far as lighter and more serious injures are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: So if it were to be the way you put it, then my conclusion is - and could you please confirm whether it is correct or not - that no one was injured by the other shells, is that correct, in view of what was written in this report.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying again, in view of what was written in this report and on the basis of what I can remember now, that's the way it was. That is what was stated in the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to move on to a document that is under seal now, and I'm aware of the time. So would it be the right time to take the break or should I move on to the other document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We could take the break. But before we do so, could I seek one matter to be clarified. Mr. Stojanovic, you took the witness to the part of the report which said that all the shells mentioned arrived from the west, from the area of Ilidza. And then you, a few lines furthers down, you said, well, here you say that this one came from Lukavica, and you noted that there was a discrepancy. Is that correctly understood by me that you saw a contradiction there?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. Perhaps there's an interpretation problem or perhaps it's the way in which I'm expressing myself. All these shells came from one direction, from Ilidza, according to this report. But the modified air bomb came from a different direction, south-west, from the direction of Lukavica. And the answer that we received was: These are two different directions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but that is clear from the report. What is the problem? Why did you -- I try to understand why you put those questions. Of course, Lukavica is not Ilidza, that's clear. But -- I -- I mean, what I'm trying to understand what your questions and what the answers of the witness added to what we see already in the report. Or just that Ilidza is not Lukavica.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this just had to do with the witness's initial answer; namely that all the projectiles had come from one direction. So this is what I put to him so that we could agree on the fact that from a elementary point of view this was not correct. So we finally got to this: That the witness agreed that this had come from two different directions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me check that for one second. Let me just see. One second, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I apologise, but I see that the witness is trying to indicate that he had something to add to the conversation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd first like to have a ... let me just see. Yes, you would say that the witness earlier said that -- he talked about both the shells and the modified air bomb. And immediately you asked him then did they all come from the same direction. And then the witness says: "From what I remember, they did. But you have the direction from which they came, all of them contained in my report." So he says, Well, find it in my report, and the report was perfectly clear on the matter. And Ilidza is not the same as Lukavica. Yes, now at least I do understand your line of questioning. Whether there was any need to further explore what was in the report is a different matter. We take a break, but could the witness be escorted out of the courtroom first, and the curtains down. If the witness would like to add something, then at the beginning of the next session he has an opportunity to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We take a break, and we'll resume at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom. Curtains down. Meanwhile, I use the opportunity to address the following matter. On the 9th of November in regard of Witness RM165, an urgent 92 ter motion was filed in which the Prosecution, in a footnote at least, says, Well, this is only 26 days between this filing and the day on which the witness is expected to give testimony. But also on the 9th and also again on the 12th of November, urgent 92 ter motions were filed - I'm referring to witnesses RM063 and RM046 - where there is only far more limited number of days between the expected day of the testimony and the day of filing of the 92 ter motion. I think the guidance was 30 days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not find anything in the footnote there, Mr. Groome. It's 11 and 9 days before.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the Prosecution apologises for that and it has to do with some scheduling problems with other witnesses and the pace that the trial is going. We fully appreciate that the Chamber could reject deciding on the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before doing so, of course we'd like to hear from the Defence. Mr. Lukic, I have raised the matter not necessarily to respond immediately but at least that you are aware that we are concerned about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Witness RM110, we'll now continue with your cross-examination. Mr. Stojanovic, if you're ready, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know if the issue remains from the previous session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Was there anything you'd like to add, Witness RM110, in relation to the questions put to you by Mr. Stojanovic and the follow-up inquires I made with Mr. Stojanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would just like to state that the first time when the Defence asked me about the direction, all I said was that it was like that, according to my best recollection. And then you said that this was in my report. So all I wanted to say, that I didn't assert that at the time. I just said that it was according to my best recollection and that only what is written in my report is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is clear, I think, also from my follow-up observations. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Before we move to it the next document, I just wanted to put one more question to you. Hrasnica and Igman, in relation to the location of the impact of the shells in Svrakino Selo, are they in the direction of south-west?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A part of them is, yes. But I don't know who was there in those sectors, who held though positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like us to look at P493. I just would like to say that this is again a document under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And therefore not to be shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Sir, can you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can we agree that this is a report drafted by a person working at the Sarajevo Security Services Centre.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can I look at page 2?

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Of course. Yes, we can look at page 2. This is not going to be broadcast in public so there will be no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at page 2 of the B/C/S version? Actually, the third page of the B/C/S version and the English version.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: You can see the name of the person who drafted the report here?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I see the name. I recognise the person. The person did work in the Security Services Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now go back to page 1 of both versions, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I'm going to put a few questions to you about this, because this is an incident that is cited in the indictment. Do you recall this incident; and do you recall going for the on-scene investigation?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say that I completely recall the incident, but judging by the document, I was there. I remember very little.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: All right. Then we can go through the text because I don't want anything to be contrary to what is written here in respect of my questions. If I read it correctly, on the 8th of October, you were informed about an incident that occurred involving fire at two trams moving along the Bascarsija-Marin Dvor or the western part route; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, it wasn't the Marin Dvor-Bascarsija route. It was vice versa, the other way around. It was the Marin Dvor-Bascarsija. It was that route.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. And then when you came to the scene, you observed that two trams were fired at, number 206 and number 236; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. That what is stated in the report.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And then you describe the incident and note - or, actually, the author, the person who drafted the report does - that first a burst of fire occurred at the -- on the 206 tram and then two or three minutes later, tram 236 was also struck. I am asking you: Were both trams moving in the same direction, going towards Bascarsija?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, this was stated based on a statement by the tram driver and that was noted by the person who drafted the report. As far as I can recall, I think that both trams were moving in the direction of Bascarsija.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: The driver's statement, the driver of the first tram, stated - and this is written in the report - that: "The aggressor's soldiers most probably fired from the Grbavica PZT or from the Metalka building." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can you please tell the Trial Chamber who stated this. Was it the tram driver or was it the officials who conducted the official investigation?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you read this sentence carefully, the beginning of the sentence, you will see that it says that the driver stated that a burst of fire was directed at the tram at 1219 hours. This something that the driver said.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Yes, that's how I understood it as well. Let me ask you this: The officials who drafted the report, did they ever note this fact or did they establish where the fire or the shots came from? Is there anything like that in the report?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is an official report. It's not a record or a transcript. The transcript or the report would be written by the investigative judge present at the investigation. But the officials, my colleagues, the person mentioned next to number 2, was -- we would not have been able to determine something like that because that is not what we were trained to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: So, based on the report, you could not conclude where the burst of fire came from.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: There's a lot of noise in our headphones.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: For the interpreters, I do not hear any noise so I'm unable to assist in tracing the source of the ...

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're having a lot of noise in our headphones. We're unable to hear what's going on in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Moloto just tells me that he moved from -- socket of the earphones from the usual place to the ones which are often used for voice distortion. I don't know whether that helps. What I do hear, I hear some noise of breathing in the -- in the earphones which often means that the speaker is nearby. But ... but that could be the witness himself, as a matter of fact. That -- perhaps could the microphone a little bit either lower or higher.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the noise is gone now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apparently the problem is resolved. The problem is resolved, Mr. Usher. Could you -- is it still okay? Could you speak a few words, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can repeat what I said earlier so that can you check the microphone, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Could I hear from the booth whether it's okay.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It's fine now. And we probably -- we believe this has nothing to do with the microphones of the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. It's fine now, so let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I think that your last answer was not recorded in the transcript so I would kindly ask you to repeat the answer. I will put the question to you again. Is it correct that you, meaning the investigation team, could not determine where the fire that was impacting tram 206 came from?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, people listed next to 2 and 3 could not have established something like that so it's not in the report. The report only refers to the statement by the driver who said that the fire came from such and such a direction and from such and such a building.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the task of the officials who drafted the official report, would that include, among other things, establishing the damage to the trams if it was caused by a burst of fire?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this damage was noted in the report. Traces of blood were found, as well as shards of glass, as well as four entry holes from the bullets.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, that is the gist of the question. This determination that you have just mentioned, does that refer to tram 206 or tram 236?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it says in the report that it was tram 236 where the traces of blood were found, as well as shards of glass.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: And the four entry holes; right?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: But I'm asking you this: Is there anything there about the damage to tram 206 in the same way that this damage was established for tram 236? Could you please look at the report and assist us on that matter.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, can I look at the second page? I don't find it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please show the witness page 2 of the document because my next question has something to do with what is on page 2.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't see anything like it. But, as I said, I did not draft the document and I really don't remember. I cannot remember all the particulars after so much time has passed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. If I were to tell you that after reading the report several times I established that the described damage was to tram 236 and that there was nothing on 206, would you agree with me, once you also read the official report?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I've re-read the report now, and your understanding of the report is your understanding. I don't see why I should be saying whether I agree with it or not, or whether you're right or not with whatever you may have concluded.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me ask you this then: Does the official report that you have in front of you establish anything at all about the direction of fire in respect of tram 236?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We will go back again to what the tram driver stated which is contained in the official report. So we have to go back to his statement about the direction of fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Did the driver of tram 236, which -- who is named in this report tell you or any other member of the on-site investigation team what he believed the direction of fire was and this somehow did not find its way into the ultimate report?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, whatever he said was recorded in the report. I don't recall that there was anything else.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Please look at the record and tell me whether it states anywhere what the direction of fire was that struck tram 236?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 1 of the B/C/S version and the English version. Can we blow up the bottom part of page 1 where the name of the driver of tram 236 is contained.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Once you've read it, I'll ask you to answer this question: Does this record state anywhere what the tram driver may have said about the direction of that burst of fire?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The driver of the second tram did not specify the direction of fire, at least not on the basis of this record.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. And am I right in saying that the on-site investigation team did not establish anything other than damage to tram 236? Am I right?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. If I were to have all the other supporting documentation in front of me, i.e., the report made by the crime-scene investigator, the sketch that they made of the crime scene, et cetera, I would perhaps be able to tell you something. Without this documentation and only on the basis of this report which is but an element of the entire forensic file, I cannot. I would have to look into the record made by the investigating judge, as well as the report produced by crime-scene examiners who were at the scene. Then I would be able to see if they established the direction of fire or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. Unfortunately, we don't have that document. Is it fair to say that reports of this sort, as a rule - and this something we will be able to see in the future documents as well - would always define the direction of fire, whether it was gun-fire, bursts of fire, or artillery fire?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, this sort of report did not necessarily have to contain all the information as the record did. This was just a preliminary report. A final report would be produced only after all the various specialists conducted their various expert examinations.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Did this official report have to contain the path or the trajectory of the entry and exit holes in the metal paneling of the tram?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Such details would normally be contained in the diagrams or sketches drawn of the crime scene by the on-site investigation members. Here, it would only be noted that they -- that some sort of damage was observed, whereas, the angle of descent or whatnot had to be defined by forensic examiners in their reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Since we don't have those reports, I will have to ask you if you do remember, and you did talk about there having been situations that were also described in official reports where the team attending the scene would check the incoming fire or the angle of descent by judging the positionings of the entry and exit holes and that this was the basis on which they determined the direction of fire? Was this the method applied in work?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were such situations because, you see, as far as I remember, none of the trams ever stopped in their tracks as soon as they were struck, because for security reasons, they had to proceed on their journey for some time still. If the security situation was good enough to allow for such sort of examination, of course, this sort of damage close to holes was carefully examined. Some sort of straw, as it were, would be threaded through the holes in order to establish what the angle was. I can't speak about these methods in greater detail than this. I only know that there were attempts at establishing the direction of fire.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Since we don't have this documentation, we only have the official report, I am trying to see how far you remember about this. Do you recall how high above ground were these four holes as described on tram 236?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Do you recall if they were level with the internal and external paneling of the tram, or were they at different heights? Were they level one with another or were they at different heights?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Let's look at page 2 of the report in both versions. I think it's page 2 in English as well. This record states, among other things, that's the beginning of paragraph 2 on page 2, which states that the scene was photographed and videoed. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Do you know, are those photographs available, as was the case with the previous instance? Can this footage be obtained? Where would they physically be located?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the crime-scene investigation department. That's where it should be. I don't know whether it is there. It should be stored in the archive.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at P3 in e-court; page 24.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness's microphones be lifted a little bit, please, thank you. Now they are too low. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Let us look at the photograph, if it can be blown up a bit. Do you recognise the photograph and the area it depicts?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can you identify the location where the trams were struck on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The street leading to the building marked with the red rectangle and the yellow building.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can I have the usher's assistance in handing the witness the pen to mark the area. Sir, to the best of your recollection, mark the approximate location of the trams that were struck in 1994 on this occasion with two circles.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give you the exact location. They were both struck in this area, on this street, one after the other, close to this building that was marked with number 3, I believe. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Please place the letter T next to that circle; T, standing for tram.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Now tell us this: Do you know where the Metalka building is located?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the neighbourhood called Grbavica.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can you identify this building called Metalka on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's precisely this building marked with a red rectangle.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, of course, that's what the photograph already says. So unless there's any dispute about whether Metalka building is the -- ask the witness to point at it, where it's already indicated in the agenda. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no dispute, I don't think, Your Honour. I only wanted for the sake of this photograph being complete in itself. I would merely like to ask the witness to mark the Metalka building with the letter M.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Which he has done by now. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Can I now ask you to mark the direction in which both trams were heading, to the best of your recollection, with an arrow?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Would you please now mark the spot where, to the best of your recollection, the UNPROFOR vehicle and UNPROFOR patrol were located.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roughly at this intersection here, where the letter -- the letter T, for tram, is drawn. How shall I put it? But it's obscured by this building here. It can't be seen.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Would the location of the UNPROFOR patrol be exposed to fire coming from the Metalka building, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the spot where I frequently saw them, they weren't that exposed. There was no optic visibility unless they were moving. If they were stationary, I don't think so. I'm telling you this on the basis of what I remember of where they were located.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Do you know if UNPROFOR troops fired back in this particular instance or in other instances where they came under fire?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in this particular case, there was no return fire. They didn't take any action. Did they normally return fire? I wouldn't be able to tell you because I never witnessed any such event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, just for my understanding, apparently you're asking questions to the witness which suggest a certain scenario. It's pretty unclear to me what scenario you're suggesting to the witness. Is it that the UNPROFOR was fired at and then would have returned fire; or was it that the -- it's -- it's unclear to me, especially the first question: Would the location of the UNPROFOR patrol be exposed to fire? Is there a suggestion that they were fired at, or possibly? And that it was stray bullets, rather, that hit the tram? Is that what you are exploring?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, in view of this witness's evidence, and you have it before you, you will see that this witness, too, spoke about situations regarding the return fire by UNPROFOR troops; also in answer to some of my questions. But I will move on. And, with your leave, I would like to tender into evidence the photograph thus marked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Page 22 of document P3, as marked by witness in court, becomes Exhibit D96 [Realtime transcript read in error "D94"], Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please. Yes, it -- P3, page 24, was asked -- Madam Registrar, you are talking about page 22 being marked or did I make a mistake? I'm looking at -- let me, again, check it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 24, by your leave, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours, [indiscernible] 22. It was page 24 of document P3, as marked by witness that becomes Exhibit D96.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And not as "D94" as recorded on line 11 of page 59. But D96.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you confirm that it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number assigned to this document is D96, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. And it was page 24 marked by the witness. Please proceed. Could you please --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to finish with these questions that have to do with this event.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: I just have to ask you one thing. If I understand this record correctly - and you tell me whether I'm right or not - you did not know which weapon was used to fire on that occasion. You just have the statement of the tram driver 206; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I've already said earlier on that the documents of the crime-scene technicians could contain the trajectory. Now I cannot recall anything else but what is stated in the official report. That is to say, that we were guided only by the statement of the driver.

utterances.speaker: MS. HOCHHAUSER
utterances.text: Thank you. And I'm not going to ask you anything else about this event because that was my understanding of it. Please allow me now to go through the official procedure that has to do with what has been called Markale II.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, with your leave, perhaps the next few questions should be put in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would have one or two questions for you, Witness. You remember that you testified about the series of projectiles that landed in the same area where the modified air bomb landed. You remember that incident?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know which incident you mean. There were several locations where I worked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You -- you testified, you remember that you have marked a photograph with where the radio and television station was, where the police station was, where a number of projectiles had fallen, and one modified aerial bomb, I think, landed on a roof. Is that clear enough for you to orient yourself to my question? Could you tell us, the projectile nearest to the police station, how far would that have approximately been to that police station, if you are able to tell us?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I cannot say anything about these measurements. We didn't even measure these distances at the time; for instance, the distance between the police station and the point of impact of the closest projectile. I don't remember us measuring that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. But even if you don't measure you know more or less whether it's the length of one football field or it's the length of five football fields, one being approximately close to 100 metres, the other one being close to 500 metres. Could you give us any -- if not, then no problem. But if you could give us any indication.

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with full certainty. But I think around 100 metres, perhaps even less. Of course, I don't know the exact distance. That would have been the distance of the closest projectile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the police station itself was not hit?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And radio and television station was not hit at that location?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, that building was not hit on this occasion. All the projectiles that I worked on that day were at this location.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, one final question. The distance of the shell landing closest to the radio and television station, you gave us an estimate on the distance on the basis of that photograph. Was there any shell which was closer to the RTV building then the one you marked on this photograph that had landed on a roof?

utterances.speaker: RM110 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there wasn't -- there wasn't one that would have been closer to the radio and television. They were all at the location where I worked. The lie of the land is such that this is at the top of the elevation which then goes downhill in the direction of the RTV building. So it's very difficult to tell on the basis of a photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for those answers. I have no further questions for you. Mr. Stojanovic, have the questions of the Bench triggered any need for further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Witness RM110, this concludes your evidence. I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for answering all the questions either put to you by the parties or the Bench, and I wish you a safe return home again. Could the curtains --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Groome -- The witness is excused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The procedural matter you would like to raise was? And we have limit the time as you see on the clock.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, last week I made mention of a lexicon. Defence and I have agreed that, although it's not complete, that it would be useful for the Chamber to have a draft. I've provided copies to the Registrar, which she is prepared to distribute in preparation for a witness later this week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: And then the other matter, Your Honour, if I could deal with in private session before the witness comes in tomorrow, that might be -- it's a simple matter but I think an important one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll hear from you tomorrow. We adjourn for the day, and we'll resume tomorrow, Tuesday, the 13th of November, at 9.30 in the morning, in this same courtroom, III.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
